title: Day 54 · Week 7, Day 5 — Protocol: the medication audit — four piles from the cabinet photos, acetaminophen against the anti-inflammatories, the three prescriptions women stop that they shouldn't, the five that get switched this week, and the one-line rule to Day 280
summary: The fourth Protocol episode, built from the bathroom-cabinet photographs taken on Day 49. Your baby is 11–13 mm at the turn into Carnegie stage 17, finger rays appearing, in the peak sensitivity window for heart, limbs and face that closes around Day 70. The baseline nobody states: 1 baby in 33 has a birth defect before anyone takes anything (CDC). How little is known: 2 of the 54 drugs women most commonly take in the first trimester have good human data (Thorpe 2013); 97.7% of drugs approved 2000–2010 had undetermined risk, taking a mean 27 years to be rated (Adam 2011). How much is taken: 81.2% of 9,459 women in 18 countries used a medicine, 47.7% paracetamol (Lupattelli 2014); first-trimester prescription use up >60% in three decades (Mitchell 2011); 28.9% used herbals (Kennedy 2013). The letters A–X are gone (FDA PLLR, 2015); MotherToBaby (866-626-6847) and UK bumps replace them. Four piles. Pile two first: acetaminophen stays first-line (the 2.48-million-child sibling study, HR 0.98; the September 2025 FDA/ACOG exchange from Day 36); NSAIDs come off the shelf — FDA 2020 bars them from 20 weeks (oligohydramnios within 48 h, reversible in 3–6 days; 30 weeks for the ductus), and the first-trimester miscarriage fight laid out in full: Quebec aOR 2.43 (4,705 cases), Israel HR 1.10 (65,457 women), Kaiser HR 1.59 and 1.45 vs acetaminophen users (1,097 women). The exception: low-dose aspirin from 12 weeks for high-risk women (USPSTF 2021 Grade B; ASPRE 4.3% → 1.6%), as question eleven on the Day 40 sheet. Pile one: the three stopped that shouldn't be — antidepressants (relapse 68% vs 26%, HR 5.0, Cohen 2006; cardiac RR 1.06 adjusted in 949,504 pregnancies; PPHN 31 vs 21 per 10,000, aOR 1.10; ACOG CPG 5 against discontinuing for pregnancy alone), asthma inhalers (LBW RR 1.46, preterm 1.41, preeclampsia 1.54 across 1.6 million; preterm excess gone with active management, RR 1.07; 20% exacerbate, 6% hospitalised; NAEPP: safer treated; budesonide, albuterol), and levothyroxine, which goes up ~30% this week (requirement +47%, from week 5–8, Alexander 2004; untreated mothers' children −7 IQ points, 19% ≤85, Haddow 1999). The switch list: ACE inhibitors/ARBs (Cooper RR 2.71; Bateman adjusted 0.89; established later-pregnancy fetopathy), warfarin (major defects OR 3.86, miscarriage 42% vs 14%, embryopathy 0.6%, window from week 8 = Day 56), valproate, isotretinoin (iPLEDGE). The OTC shelf by fact sheet: loratadine and cetirizine fine; pseudoephedrine waits (gastroschisis OR 1.8, 4.2 with acetaminophen, null in 2009; baseline 1 in 2,564); dextromethorphan fine; calcium carbonate fine two hours from iron; bismuth subsalicylate out; topical tretinoin out despite reassuring small cohorts. Pile three: vitamin A >10,000 IU PR 4.8, 1 in 57 (Rothman 1995), retinol capsules go, kelp goes, herbals treated as drugs without data. Pile four: your ibuprofen in your drawer. The rule: nothing new without the call, nothing stopped without it. The audit sheet and the hotline number.
action: Fifteen minutes tonight with the Day 49 photographs and one sheet. Four headings — hers daily, hers as needed, supplements, mine — and every name with its dose. Then three marks: a tick beside acetaminophen, the prenatal and anything the fact sheets cleared; a circle beside every daily prescription and anything on the switch list (ACE inhibitors/ARBs, warfarin, valproate, isotretinoin), with the prescriber's name — those are tomorrow morning's calls, levothyroxine or warfarin first; a line through ibuprofen, naproxen, bismuth subsalicylate, any retinol capsule, the retinoid cream and kelp, which go into a bag in your drawer. Save MotherToBaby, 866-626-6847 (or medicinesinpregnancy.org in the UK), in both phones as 'can she take this'. File the sheet behind the Day 40 question list and add question eleven: is she a low-dose aspirin candidate from 12 weeks?
